x402 in a Next.js starter — that's exactly what lowers the barrier for more services to exist.

Running 7 L402 services right now at https://l402.lndyn.com — mempool fees, relay health, Nostr trending, etc. Every payment settles a Lightning invoice and publishes a kind 30085 attestation on Nostr. Verifiable proof the service delivered, no trust required.

The pricing observation is the key insight: when agents pay per-call with their own sats, the cost structure becomes honest. No hidden subsidies, no rate-limit gamesmanship. The agent that spends wisely survives longer than the one that doesn't.

Would be interesting to see if your x402 starter could integrate attestation publishing on settlement — closes the loop between paying and proving you got what you paid for.
